[[File:Great ditrigonal icosidodecahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great ditrigonal icosidodecahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''great ditrigonal icosidodecahedron''' (or '''great ditrigonary icosidodecahedron''') is a [[nonconvex uniform polyhedron]], indexed as U<sub>47</sub>. It has 32 faces (20 [[triangle]]s and 12 [[pentagon]]s), 60 edges, and 20 vertices.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathconsult.ch/static/unipoly/47.html|title=47: great ditrigonal icosidodecahedron|last=Maeder|first=Roman|date=|website=MathConsult|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> It has 4 [[Schwarz triangle]] equivalent constructions, for example [[Wythoff symbol]] '''3 | 3 {{Frac|5|4}}''' gives [[Coxeter diagram]] {{CDD||label5-4|branch_10ru|split2|node}} = {{CDD|node_h3|5-2|node|3|node}}. It has extended [[Schläfli symbol]] a&lbrace;{{Frac|5|2}},3} or c{3,{{Frac|5|2}}}, as an ''altered great stellated dodecahedron'' or ''converted great icosahedron''.

Its [[circumradius]] is <math display=inline>\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</math> times the length of its edge,<ref name=Weisstein2003>{{Citation
 | last = Weisstein | first =  Eric W
 | year = 2003
 | title = CRC concise encyclopedia of mathematics
 | isbn = 1-58488-347-2
 | publisher = Chapman & Hall/CRC
 | location = Boca Raton
}}</ref> a value it shares with the [[cube]].

== Related polyhedra ==

Its [[convex hull]] is a regular [[dodecahedron]]. It additionally shares its [[edge arrangement]] with the [[small ditrigonal icosidodecahedron]] (having the triangular faces in common), the [[ditrigonal dodecadodecahedron]] (having the pentagonal faces in common), and the regular [[compound of five cubes]].
